You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: The module encodes and solves the Car Talk balance-scale puzzle: given a stone of weight W pounds and a balance scale, find N pieces whose weights allow any integer weight from 1 to W to be measured. Because pieces may be placed on either side of the scale, each piece contributes a coefficient of −1, 0, or +1, so the problem reduces to finding a sequence of N positive integers summing to W such that every integer in 1..W can be expressed as a signed combination of those integers.

The module defines two key operators. `Partitions(seq, wt)` recursively enumerates all non-decreasing sequences of N natural numbers that sum to W, pruning the search using tight bounds on valid element ranges. `Weighs(seq, wt)` checks whether a given partition can represent a target weight by existentially quantifying over coefficient assignments from {−1, 0, 1} applied to each piece. The central `ASSUME` statement directs TLC to search all such ordered partitions and, for each one, test whether every weight in 1..W is achievable; if a valid partition is found, it is printed via `PrintT`; otherwise the string "No solution" is printed. The module has no variables, no state transitions, and no temporal properties — it is purely a model-checking computation wrapper that exploits TLC's assumption-evaluation mechanism to solve a combinatorial puzzle, with the default configuration setting W = 40 and N = 4.
